answer: A single mirror checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a terrace, before it can post or attest. Forging 244 aliases as a result costs 275 bonds held for 9 days each, plus the haven attestations those aliases can never earn. That is 24 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
